text:
incident-bot: ALERT fired: routing-fallback-loop detected across regions (us-east <-> us-west <-> eu). Severity: P1

sarah (oncall): got the page, i'm on it. what services are impacted?

kevin (eng-runtime): routing-controller is rapidly moving traffic between regional variants. we see repeated probe failures triggering immediate fallback swaps.

olivia (support): customers in EU report elevated latency and occasional 502/504s since 00:06 UTC. Support queue +1 escalated customer.

marco (sre): graphs: probe-health series shows ~25-40s oscillation. correlation with a routing policy push at 00:04 UTC. possible policy regress.

kevin (eng-runtime): we rolled a new fallback-policy that lowered the probe failure threshold and enabled instant cross-region failover. bad combo with noisy probes.

sarah (oncall): can we stop the churn quickly (customer impact) — propose two-step: freeze routing-policy, reduce probe concurrency.

marco (sre): ack. temp mitigation: scale health-probers to 1 replica and set probe-interval to 10s in the live config to reduce thrash.

kevin (eng-runtime): i'm initiating rollback to last-known-good policy (commit: d4c9e1). executing now.

devops-bot: ROLLBACK STARTED by kevin (eng-runtime) -> routing/policies@d4c9e1

devops-bot: ROLLBACK COMPLETE -> policy reconciled to d4c9e1 (rolling update done)

marco (sre): scaled prober and lowered concurrency. monitoring for stabilization.

incident-bot: metric update: region eu 5xx rate decreased 35% within 90s of rollback.

olivia (support): customer update drafted: "We're investigating intermittent errors affecting some requests in EU. We've deployed a mitigation and are monitoring. We'll follow up with a detailed timeline." Sending now.

kevin (eng-runtime): extracted timeline from controller logs:
```
00:04:01 policy-apply: new-fallback-policy v7 -> min_failures=1, immediate_swap=true
00:04:10 probe: eu -> reported unhealthy
00:04:12 route-swap: eu -> us-west
00:04:35 probe: us-west -> unhealthy
00:04:36 route-swap: us-west -> us-east
```

kevin (eng-runtime): hypothesis: policy allowed a single probe failure to trigger swap, probes occasionally return transient failures -> created three-way ping-pong.

sarah (oncall): agreed root cause hypothesis. next actions: (1) add hysteresis to fallback policy (require N consecutive failures), (2) add cooldown window, (3) improve probe reporting (reason codes).

marco (sre): i'll open a follow-up with immediate alert tuning: bump unhealthy-window to 90s for 30m and silence repeated flapping paging to oncall for identical symptom for next 10m.

kevin (eng-runtime): i'll prepare a canary PR for policy changes: set min_failures=2 and cooldown_seconds=120. will run against probe-sim locally then canary in us-west for 10% traffic.

sarah (oncall): good. hold off on re-enabling cross-region instant fallback until canary validated for 15m.

incident-bot: PAGING reminder -> handoff scheduled: sarah -> kevin in 25m

olivia (support): support: 2 remaining active cases; assigned severity=degraded, customers notified.

marco (sre): metrics trending back to baseline. latency improved in eu. will keep longer retention for routing controller traces for next 2 hours.

kevin (eng-runtime): PR: https://git.internal/redwood/routing/pulls/482 (draft) with cooldown + hysteresis. tagging marco for review.

sarah (oncall): i'm marking this as mitigated for now, keeping incident open for postmortem. please capture timeline in the incident doc.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS -> MITIGATED (P1 -> P2). follow-up tasks created: routing-policy: add hysteresis + canary rollout; improve probe diagnostics.

kevin (eng-runtime): taking over watch. if flapping recurs i'll temporarily pin per-region variants to avoid cross-region swaps.

marco (sre): set temporary alert suppression rule and increased unhealthy-window on production for 30m.

olivia (support): will follow up with impacted customers after postmortem.

sarah (oncall): thanks all. great quick coordination. closing this thread and moving notes to /incidents/postmortem-1719007777.

incident-bot: THREAD ARCHIVE NOTE: participants: sarah (oncall), kevin (eng-runtime), marco (sre), olivia (support), devops-bot, incident-bot
